item.title: 52 days to election: Orbán escalates Ukraine row, AI execution video shocks Hungary’s election campaign
item.description: In this week's digest from the Hungarian election campaign trail: Ukraine oil rows, Viktor Orban vows to finish off the job against civil society and independent media after April election and accuses the Shell oil company of being behind the opposition.

item.title: Top European AI boss warns of US tech concentration at India summit
item.description: The CEO of Paris-based Mistral, often touted as a European AI champion, raised concerns over the concentration of AI power in a few companies during the global summit in India, while political leaders focused on tech safety.

item.title: Poland’s Sikorski says the quiet bit out loud: Europe has become Ukraine’s lifeline, not US
item.description: Last year, Europe became Ukraine’s main supporter, providing over $200bn (€170bn) in military, financial, and humanitarian aid, while US assistance dropped sharply, shifting the war’s centre of gravity to the EU.

item.title: What it means for Europe’s energy prices and refugees if Trump attacks Iran
item.description: Iran’s population today exceeds 93 million— and is hosts six million Afghan refugees. In the event of regional war, both Iranians and displaced Afghans would inevitably seek routes toward Europe.

item.title: Listen: Should the EU stay away from Trump’s Board of Peace?
item.description: In Brussels, several EU member states are angry with the European Commission. These countries did not appreciate that the EU’s executive body attended the first meeting of the “Board of Peace” launched by Donald Trump. What was the alternative for the EU? Should Europeans stay away from this initiative?

item.title: MEPs delay vote on deportation bill to March amid return hubs dispute
item.description: "We aim to work from the political centre and build constructive, workable compromises," said the office of Malik Azmani, a Dutch liberal from the Renew Europe faction, who is leading talks on the bill.

item.title: EU set to push for WTO reform at Cameroon summit in March
item.description: The EU and US are pushing for reform of the WTO's most favoured nation principle which is supposed to offer tariff and quota free trade.

item.title: Orbán bashes Ukraine on Nord Stream, as Trump tells Hungarians how to vote
item.description: Hungary’s prime minister Viktor Orbán accused Ukraine of blowing up Nord Stream, amplifying anti-Ukrainian rhetoric ahead of elections, amid EU-Russia sanctions talks and disputes over Russian oil and diesel deliveries.

item.title: From a digital Wild West to strict age limits: do social-media bans actually protect teens?
item.description: Many EU member states are working on social media bans individually, before any EU-wide measure — but is banning social media, only for kids, and one country at a time, the best move?

item.title: THIS WEEK: Clock is ticking for Russian sanctions deal in time for Ukraine war anniversary
item.description: Fourth-anniversary Russian sanctions, plans for Gaza under Donald Trump's Board of Peace, Friedrich Merz in China, and domestic EU curbs on firearms are all on the table this week.
